title: For two hours, for a week

blocks.text: “How long?” — the accusative, with no preposition.

items.text: In expressions answering the questions „How long?“ and „How long ago?“ the accusative case is used: Я был там год. Я был там месяц. Я был там неделю.

blocks.text: DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 41. One sentence at a time, in a new order each time you open this chapter; it is finished when every one has been answered right. The sentences are real: the source of each is shown with it.

exercises.q: Ехать полтора ___ (час, gen. sg.) на работу — тягомотина.
exercises.prompt: Driving for one and a half hours to get to work is a bear.
exercises.why: **полтора часа** — полтора (полторы with a feminine noun) takes the genitive singular, like 2–4 (час → часа).

exercises.q: Я пробуду в Баку три ___ (неделя, gen. sg.).
exercises.prompt: I will stay in Baku for three weeks.
exercises.why: **три недели** — 2–4, 22–24, 32–34… (not 12–14) take the genitive singular (неделя → недели).

exercises.q: Я жила в Ванкувере два ___ (месяц, gen. sg.).
exercises.prompt: I lived in Vancouver for two months.
exercises.why: **два месяца** — 2–4, 22–24, 32–34… (not 12–14) take the genitive singular (месяц → месяца).
**три дня** — 2–4, 22–24, 32–34… (not 12–14) take the genitive singular (день → дня).
**три часа** — 2–4, 22–24, 32–34… (not 12–14) take the genitive singular (час → часа).

exercises.prompt: The pass is valid for two weeks.
exercises.why: **две недели** — 2–4, 22–24, 32–34… (not 12–14) take the genitive singular (неделя → недели).
